title: TS SDK: runtime output validators and developer patterns for discriminated structured outputs
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: SDK consumers need a predictable, ergonomically-typed surface for structured outputs coming from the API. Current gaps: (1) generated TypeScript types are brittle for discriminated unions produced by function/tool calling or structured output contracts; (2) runtime validation helpers (Zod/JSON-schema) are scattered and inconsistent across examples; (3) streaming responses complicate validator usage because partial chunks may not form a valid discriminated shape until the stream ends.

Goal: Provide a canonical pattern and runtime helpers in the TS SDK that: generate interoperable TypeScript types from our output contract schemas, emit companion Zod validators and JSON Schema artifacts, and offer streaming-safe validator utilities that can validate incremental chunks and final merged output. Deliverables should include examples, docs, and a migration path for internal consumers and customers using earlier SDK versions.
acceptance_criteria: A codegen pipeline task that produces: TypeScript .d.ts types, a Zod schema file, and a JSON Schema file from our structured-output contract artifacts
Runtime helpers in the TS SDK that expose: validateResponse(obj) -> {ok|err, errors}, streamingValidator(bufferChunk) -> {partialOk|needsMore|finalOk|errors}
Discriminated-union patterns documented with examples for: tool/function-calling outputs, multi-variant completion outputs, and nested discriminators
Migration guide for existing consumers showing minimum-breaking changes and helper shims
Integration tests covering codegen -> runtime validation cycle, streaming chunk assembly, and backward-compatible resolver behavior
A referenced GitHub PR with implementation and a follow-up RFC linked in docs
scope_notes: This ticket focuses on TypeScript SDK artifacts and runtime helpers. Python/Go SDK teams should be notified (email + doc) but separate tickets will own language-specific artifacts. Not addressing compile-time-only helpers that require build-step plugins (those will be considered in a separate RFC).
out_of_scope: Implementing identical streaming validator APIs for Python/Go (tracked separately). Rewriting the existing server-side contract DSL — we only consume exported schema artifacts.
tasks: Define canonical output-contract -> [TS types, Zod schema, JSON Schema] mapping and add to codegen spec
Create runtime helpers package @redwood/sdk-output-validators with validateResponse and streaming helpers
Author examples in examples/structured-output: simple discriminator, nested discriminator, streaming completion example
Add integration tests in sdk/__tests__/output-validators.test.ts covering merging streamed chunks and final validation
Document migration guide and patterns in docs/ts-sdk/structured-output.md
Add canary release of runtime helpers behind feature flag and monitor errors (sentry tag: sdk-output-validators)
Collect feedback from Design (Review UX for error messages) and PM on acceptability tradeoffs
risks: Type/validator mismatch between codegen output and runtime behavior if contract DSL changes without versioning
Performance regression for high-throughput streaming endpoints if validators do naive re-parse on every chunk
Developer confusion if both Zod and JSON Schema helpers are offered without clear guidance on when to use each
implementation_notes: Proposed approach: codegen emits a stable artifact bundle per contract: <contract>.types.d.ts, <contract>.zod.ts, <contract>.jsonschema.json. The runtime package will import the .zod file to provide validators. For streaming, implement a small stateful 'chunk-accumulator' that applies permissive partial-parsing rules: 1) accept/record parseable discriminator fields early; 2) attempt partial Zod.parse when stable fields present; 3) defer final validation until stream close; provide a strict finalValidate() call. Ensure helpers are tree-shakeable.
notes: Design feedback (2025-02-25): prefer human-readable, actionable error messages rather than Zod's raw errors. Action: add error-formatter util.
PM feedback (2025-02-26): expose a lightweight shim for existing consumers to opt-in without codegen changes.
Infra note: codegen will run in CI; output artifacts should be checked into packages/sdk-output-contracts to avoid drift in releases.
RFC draft for broader codegen conventions: https://docs.internal.redwood.ai/rfcs/0008-output-codegen
updates: 2025-02-20: Kickoff meeting with Eng, PM, and Design. Agreement to support both Zod and JSON Schema outputs; prioritized Zod for runtime validators.
2025-02-24: Initial codegen prototype produced sample zod file for 'email-summarize' contract. Found two edge cases with nested discriminators.
2025-02-28: Implemented streaming chunk accumulator prototype and micro-benchmark; initial results show <5% overhead for 1k RPS when using incremental checks.
2025-03-03: UX review done — added plan for formatted errors and error codes. Preparing PR for runtime helpers and example suite.
2025-03-04: Opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3547 containing runtime helpers and tests. Requesting eng review from Marco Alvarez and Design review from Aisha Kapoor.
final_notes: If accepted, follow-up tickets will split Python/Go validator parity and a minor release to roll helpers out behind a runtime flag. Monitor customer error rates for first two weeks after release and collect migration issues from SDK Slack channel.
